# Dashboard data access for per-project quota and consumption

## Description

This epic delivers the Dashboard-side data-access layer that reads each
project's Kueue quota (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue) and current consumption so the
administrator chargeback view can render a per-project comparison. It works
against existing, stable platform interfaces (Kueue CRs and exposed metrics per
the Distributed Workloads architecture context) and is deliberately independent
of the GPU-hour metering data delivered by the separate in-flight metering
strategy — this work must not wait on that schema.

## Scope

- Read per-project Kueue quota (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue) and current
  utilization from the existing Kueue CRs/metrics interfaces
- Expose the quota and current consumption data to the Dashboard admin view
  layer (backend API/layer within the odh-dashboard codebase)
- Keep the surface generic enough that per-project GPU-hour totals from the
  metering-backed reporting backend can be joined in later without rework

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with a Kueue quota, the Dashboard backend can retrieve that
  quota and its current consumption
- The data-access layer does not depend on the metering data schema owned by
  the separate metering strategy (that data is joined in by the follow-up
  GPU-hour totals presentation epic, not here)
- No re-implementation of metering collection (explicitly out of scope for
  this strategy)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against
  each project's Kueue quota — this epic provides the data access that view
  builds on

# Per-project GPU-hour reporting backend with CSV export and stable API

## Description

This epic delivers the reporting backend that computes per-project GPU-hour
consumption reports over selectable time ranges from the metering data
delivered by the separate in-flight GPU usage metering strategy, and exposes
them for export as CSV and via a stable API for finance tooling. It consumes
the metering data; it does not re-implement collection.

**External dependency / Tier 2**: the metering data schema is owned by the
metering strategy and is not final until that strategy lands. This epic is
gated on that schema being final. The reporting backend builds against the
finalized schema contract.

## Scope

- Compute per-project GPU-hour consumption aggregates over selectable time
  ranges from the delivered metering data
- CSV export of the reports
- Stable API for retrieving reports, suitable for finance tooling integration
- Validation of the draft metering data contract against reporting needs
  (aggregation keys, time-bucketing, per-project attribution) before
  implementation locks in — recorded as an acceptance criterion below, not a
  separate investigation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can retrieve per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  selectable time ranges, computed from the delivered metering data
- Reports can be exported as CSV
- Reports are retrievable via a stable API documented for finance tooling
- The metering data contract (as delivered by the metering strategy) has been
  validated against the aggregation, time-bucketing, and per-project
  attribution needs of the reports before the implementation is finalized
- Metering collection is consumed, never re-implemented (out of scope for this
  strategy)
- Reports are denominated in GPU-hours; no currency/cost-rate modelling (out of
  scope)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges computed from the metering data
- HLR-2 (P1): CSV export and stable API retrieval for finance tooling (bundled
  here — same data structures and API endpoints as HLR-1)

# Dashboard presentation of per-project GPU-hour totals from the reporting backend

## Description

This epic delivers the Tier 2 Dashboard-side presentation of per-project
GPU-hour consumption totals retrieved from the metering-backed reporting
backend, shown in the administrator view alongside the quota comparison. It is
split out of the Tier 1 admin view work so that the quota comparison ships
independently of the external metering schema timing: this epic consumes the
reporting backend's stable API, so it is Tier 2 — gated on both the external
metering data schema being final (the reporting backend cannot deliver its API
before that) and on that API contract existing.

It has two prerequisites, both expressed as DAG edges:

- the quota/consumption view work (this epic adds a column to the admin view
  it delivers), and
- the metering-backed reporting backend with CSV export and stable API (this
  epic is a consumer of that API — it cannot be built or tested until the
  contract exists).

## Scope

- Extend the administrator Dashboard view to show, per project, the
  per-project GPU-hour totals retrieved from the reporting backend's stable
  API, alongside the existing quota/consumption comparison
- Integrate the reporting backend's API as the data source for these totals
  (consume the API; do not re-implement report computation or metering
  collection)
- Preserve the Tier 1 behavior of the admin view when the reporting backend
  is unavailable (the quota comparison remains functional without the
  GPU-hour column)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the reporting backend's stable API is available, the administrator
  Dashboard view shows, per project, the per-project GPU-hour totals
  retrieved from that API alongside the Kueue quota comparison
- The GPU-hour totals column is populated from the reporting backend's
  documented stable API (not a bespoke data path), and metering collection /
  report computation is not re-implemented on the Dashboard side
- When the reporting backend or its API is unavailable, the admin view still
  renders the per-project quota comparison without the GPU-hour totals
  column and without errors (graceful degradation)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): the Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption
  against each project's Kueue quota — this epic extends that view with the
  per-project GPU-hour totals from the reporting backend. HLR-3 is the only
  HLR this epic maps to, so it inherits P1; it is a consumer of the P0
  reporting surface, not an enabler of P0 work
